comparison_equation_labels: SP-125 Eq. (4-23) Sieder-Tate coolant-side Nusselt relation
supports_model.mismatch_notes: SP-125 (the registry's local source) prints Nu = C1 Re^0.8 Pr^0.4 (mu/mu_w)^0.14 with a coolant-specific C1 (RP-1: 0.0214, PDF p.119). The code and registry use 0.027 Re^0.8 Pr^(1/3) (mu_b/mu_w)^0.14 (the classical Sieder & Tate 1936 form, which is not held in the corpus). Same structure and viscosity correction; different coefficient and Prandtl exponent. Relative to the SP-125 RP-1 form the code's h_c is higher by about 26% at Pr = 1, 17% at Pr = 3 and 7% at Pr = 11.7 (RP-1 at 600 R).

model_review.citation_vs_support: BAD_ATTRIBUTION for the coefficients: the registry's local source (NASA SP-125) does not state 0.027 or Pr^(1/3); it states Pr^0.4 with a coolant-specific C1. The code docstring also cites Sieder & Tate (Ind. Eng. Chem. 28, 1936), which is not in the corpus.
model_review.execution_reach: Not measured; the MDO cooling march uses sieder_tate_hc for the coolant side.
model_review.sensitivity: Coolant-side h_c +7% to +26% versus SP-125's RP-1 calibration lowers predicted wall temperatures (non-conservative direction).
model_review.physics_finding: Owner decision required (code edits are outside this session's scope): adopt SP-125 Eq. 4-23 with coolant-specific C1 (RP-1 = 0.0214, page-verified), or acquire Sieder & Tate (1936) to support 0.027 and Pr^(1/3); coolant-specific constants are missing for methane and hydrogen.
remaining_uncertainties: entrance-length and curvature effects not represented
supercritical and boiling regimes need separate models (Eq. 4-24, 4-25; Nasuti Eq. 9)

equations.quote: for turbulent heat transfer to liquids flowing in channels
equations.description: Turbulent heat transfer to liquids in channels; C1 is a constant with different values for various coolants; Nu = h_c d/k, Re = rho V_co d/mu, Pr = mu C_p/k, mu at bulk and mu_w at coolant-side wall temperature.
validity: nonboiling subcritical-temperature regions at subcritical and supercritical coolant pressure (A1-A2, B1-B2 of Fig. 4-27)
